<translate>
<code>config/dragonminez/entities.json</code> sets the base stats of DMZ creatures and enemies, and the default stat jump when a saga enemy transforms into its next form. Like the other server configs, the server sends it to every client.
</translate>

<translate>
For the creatures themselves, see the [[Special:MyLanguage/Bestiary|Bestiary]].
</translate>

<translate>
== Keys ==
</translate>
{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Key</translate> !! <translate>Default</translate> !! <translate>What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>configVersion</code> || <translate>A version string, for example <code>"2.2.0"</code></translate> || <translate>Version stamp used for config upgrades. Do not change it (see [[Special:MyLanguage/How to JSON|How to JSON]]).</translate>
|-
| <code>defaultEntityStats</code> || <translate>See below</translate> || <translate>Base stats per entity id (an object).</translate>
|-
| <code>transformDefaults</code> || <translate>See below</translate> || <translate>Default multipliers and trigger used when a saga enemy transforms (an object).</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Entity base stats ==
</translate>
{{See also|Bestiary|Custom Quests}}
<translate>
<code>defaultEntityStats</code> maps an entity registry id (for example <code>"dragonminez:bandit"</code>) to a stat object:
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Key</translate> !! <translate>Default</translate> !! <translate>What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>health</code> || <code>20</code> || <translate>Max health. The default applies when the field is missing.</translate>
|-
| <code>meleeDamage</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate>Melee attack damage. The default applies when the field is missing.</translate>
|-
| <code>kiDamage</code> || <code>1</code> || <translate>Ki blast damage (only for entities that have a ki blast damage attribute). The default applies when the field is missing.</translate>
|}

<translate>
Values below <code>1</code> are raised to <code>1</code>.
</translate>

<translate>
The stats are applied once, when the entity first spawns. Entities that were already in the world keep the stats they spawned with. Entities spawned for a quest use the stats written in the quest instead (see [[Special:MyLanguage/Custom Quests|Custom Quests]]), scaled by the difficulty multipliers in [[Special:MyLanguage/General Server Config|General Server Config]] (<code>easyMode*</code> / <code>hardMode*</code>); naturally spawned entities are not scaled by difficulty.
</translate>

<translate>
You can add entries for other entity ids too: any living entity whose id is listed gets these stats when it spawns.
</translate>

<translate>
== Spawn rates ==
</translate>
{{See also|Bestiary}}
<translate>
<code>entities.json</code> only sets stats. Where and how often creatures spawn naturally is defined by the Forge biome modifiers in <code>data/dragonminez/forge/biome_modifier/</code> (spawn weights and group sizes per biome), which a datapack can override.
</translate>

<translate>
Bandits, the Red Ribbon Army, Sabertooth Tigers, Frieza's Soldiers and Mini Buus use their own spawn category, <code>dragonminez:wild_enemy</code>, with its own cap. Structures can define spawns for it in their <code>spawn_overrides</code>, as the [[Special:MyLanguage/Red Ribbon Tower|Red Ribbon Tower]] does. The spawn rules, weights and biomes of each creature are listed in the [[Special:MyLanguage/Bestiary|Bestiary]].
</translate>

<translate>
== Saga enemy transformations ==
</translate>
{{See also|Sagas}}
<translate>
Saga enemies that have a next form (for example Frieza) transform when their health drops low enough. The <code>transformDefaults</code> values are used unless the quest's kill objective sets its own.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Key</translate> !! <translate>Default</translate> !! <translate>What it does</translate>
|-
| <code>healthMultiplier</code> || <code>1.5</code> || <translate>The new form's max health is the previous form's max health × this value (minimum <code>0.1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>meleeMultiplier</code> || <code>1.5</code> || <translate>Multiplier on the previous form's melee damage (minimum <code>0.1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>kiMultiplier</code> || <code>1.5</code> || <translate>Multiplier on the previous form's ki blast damage (minimum <code>0.1</code>).</translate>
|-
| <code>triggerHealthPercent</code> || <code>0.5</code> || <translate>Fraction of max health (<code>0</code>–<code>1</code>) at which the enemy transforms.</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Example ==
</translate>
<syntaxhighlight lang="json">
{
  "configVersion": "2.2.0",
  "defaultEntityStats": {
    "dragonminez:bandit": {
      "health": 75.0,
      "meleeDamage": 10.0,
      "kiDamage": 0.0
    }
  },
  "transformDefaults": {
    "healthMultiplier": 1.5,
    "meleeMultiplier": 1.5,
    "kiMultiplier": 1.5,
    "triggerHealthPercent": 0.5
  }
}
</syntaxhighlight>

<translate>
== Removed keys ==
</translate>
<translate>
<code>hardModeSettings</code> (<code>hpMultiplier</code>, <code>damageMultiplier</code>) no longer exists. Difficulty scaling is configured in [[Special:MyLanguage/General Server Config|General Server Config]] with <code>easyModeHPMultiplier</code>, <code>easyModeDamageMultiplier</code>, <code>hardModeHPMultiplier</code> and <code>hardModeDamageMultiplier</code>.
</translate>

<translate>
== Reload and validate ==
</translate>
{{See also|Reloading and Updating Changes|How to JSON}}
<translate>
# Edit <code>config/dragonminez/entities.json</code>.
# Validate the JSON syntax.
# Run <code>/dmzreload config</code>. New values apply to entities spawned afterwards.
</translate>
